requirements.requirement: Expose node1's staged projects directory as an SMB share named projects for the design team.
requirements.summary: Node1 has a valid projects-only Samba configuration, an active and enabled SMB service listening on 10.100.1.10:445, and node2 successfully enumerated the projects share. Final checks after restart confirmed the configuration and service remained healthy.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to list, read, and update documents as designer using the credentials in access.txt.
requirements.summary: Commands parsed the designer credentials from access.txt and directly demonstrated authenticated listing, hash-verified reads, file creation, overwrite, read-back, and post-restart write/delete behavior from node2.

requirements.requirement: Reject guest access and access to sibling directories.
requirements.summary: Anonymous enumeration and project access returned ACCESS_DENIED. Authenticated access to the unshared private sibling returned BAD_NETWORK_NAME, and attempted traversal to private/contracts.txt was rejected. These denials were also observed after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Keep the initial drawings in /srv/legacy2/samba-team-share intact.
requirements.summary: Final SHA-256 hashes for drawing.txt and materials.csv exactly match the preparation baseline; the protected sibling contracts file also remained unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after execution and restart. Samba 4.23.5 packages came from the configured RHEL 10 repositories.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered services, data, security state, and SMB workflow.
limitations: Credential values were appropriately redacted, so the exact password cannot be independently inspected; evidence nevertheless shows the commands read access.txt and then authenticated successfully from node2.

The first node1 post-restart client recovery script exited nonzero because of its deletion-check logic, although its output directly shows successful read, write, and read-back operations; subsequent evidence confirmed cleanup and a fully healthy end-to-end workflow.
Lifecycle snapshots provide bounded inventories rather than complete filesystem and configuration captures; detailed task-specific commands supply the remaining direct evidence.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command review. Package installation and the node2 RPM-key import were necessary prerequisites; account, permission, Samba, SELinux, firewall, and service changes directly implemented the share. Test writes supported behavioral verification and temporary artifacts were removed. The failed initial node2 package attempt downloaded packages subsequently reused by the successful installation. Failed cleanup/audit scripts did not leave lasting residue, and cmd-f38ff0f7700f4319 removed the two discovered temporary downloads. The secured default-configuration backup has a clear rollback purpose. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package state, no executor test files under /tmp, and only the intended node1 SMB listener.
